1.

Apprehending arrest in connection with Crime No.94 of 2021, registered at Police Station Jashpur, District - Jashpur (C.G.) for +0530 offence punishable under Section 420, 109, 376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, the applicants have preferred this application for grant of anticipatory bail.
2. Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that on 18.1.2019 the complainant was married to Manish Soni and after marriage, she started residing in her matrimonial home in Jamshedpur.

From initial days of marriage, members of in-laws family of complainant started harassing her for demand of Vinod Soni vs The State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109096450/

sentences.text: When the complainant conceived pregnancy, she was compelled by her husband to abort her pregnancy on the ground that he does not want child at that moment.

The complainant returned to her parents' house in January, 2020 and thereafter complaint was lodged based upon which instant crime is registered on 26.4.2021 against present applicants and three others i.e. sister-in-law, mother-in-law and husband of complainant.
Initially the charge-sheet was submitted by investigating agency for commission of offence under Section 498A, 494, 495 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

While framing charge, the learned trial Court has also framed charges under Section 376 read with Section 109 of I.P.C.
3.
Learned counsel for applicants submits that based on the complaint initially a crime was registered under Section 494, 498-A, 495 and 420 of I.P.C..
After registration of crime, applicants have approached this Court by way of filing an application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., which was allowed vide order dated 29.07.2021.
Applicants are father-in-law and brother-in-law of complainant.
The allegation by complainant in the FIR is that suppressing the earlier marriage of co- accused Manish Soni, his marriage was performed with complainant.

As the charges under Section 376 read with Section 109 are framed against applicants, they are apprehending their arrest and therefore, applicants have approached before this court by way of filing this subsequent application for grant of anticipatory bail.

There is no role of applicants in commission of alleged crime if any under Section 376 read with Section 109 of I.P.C.
4.
Per contra learned State counsel opposes the application for grant of bail and the submission made in this respect.
It is submitted that suppressing the earlier marriage of co-accused Manish Soni applicants have performed his marriage with complainant.

However, he do not dispute submission of learned counsel for applicants with respect to grant of anticipatory bail to applicants in M.Cr.C.(A) No.829 of 2021 in the above crime and the offence under Section 376 read with Section 109 of I.P.C. is added later on at the time of framing of charge.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary and the documents.

6. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegation, applicants were already granted benefit of anticipatory bail in M.Cr.C.(A) No. 829 of 2021 vide order dated 29.07.2021 and there is no direct allegation against applicants for commission of sexual intercourse with the complainant, without commenting anything on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to extend the benefit of Section 482 of B.N.S. to the applicants 7.
Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application filed under Section 482 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is allowed.

8. It is directed that in the event of arrest of the applicants in connection with the aforesaid offence,
they shall be released on bail by the officer arresting them on executing a personal bond in sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety each in the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer.
